# RECORDED 2026-08-27. THE SAME MACHINE as dkms-status-mixed.txt, asked
#
#     dkms status -k 9.9.9-99-generic
#
# a kernel it has no builds for at all. Exit code 0.
#
# `-k` DID NOT FILTER AND DID NOT ANSWER ABOUT THAT KERNEL. It dropped the
# kernel and architecture columns from every row and left three modules reading
# `added` -- including `good`, which is installed for 7.0.0-30-generic, and
# `bad`, whose build failed. A gate that ran `dkms status -k $newKernel` and
# looked for something wrong would find nothing here, on a machine where
# nothing has been built for $newKernel at all.
bad/3.0: added
good/1.0: added
half/2.0: added
